The grader is a model, not a person. qwen3.8-27b graded every answer. The 25-question spot-check sheet (bench/spotcheck_v1.md) is there so a person can measure how often it is wrong; that audit has not been done yet.

Generated questions are easier than real ones. Most are written from a single section and name their subject. Real users ask vaguer questions. The overview (15) and two-section (22) groups are small, so their percentages move a lot with one or two answers.

Some gold labels were wrong. 4 of 30 questions the generator called unanswerable are in fact answered by the document (for example, the Transformer paper does say it trained on 8 P100 GPUs). An audit step found them and they are excluded from all numbers above.

The benchmark found a real bug, now fixed. Asked across the whole library, an overview question used the first six documents instead of the one it named. Before the fix, overview accuracy was 27%; the numbers above are after the fix, with the overview questions re-run.

Where plain RAG does better. On two-section questions (73% vs 86%) and on unanswerable questions (77% vs 85%) our system is behind. In the unanswerable failures, the answer model filled the gap from its own general knowledge; the citation check flagged some of those sentences as only partly supported, but not all.

OCR on damaged Indic scans. On the medium-damage Hindi scan, Tesseract reported high confidence (79) while getting 13% of characters wrong, so the page was never sent to the vision model. On the heavy-damage Hindi scan, even the vision model got 70% wrong. English scans recover fully.
Speed depends on the API tier. Times were measured on Groq's paid tier. On the free tier, rate limits stretch a typical answer to about 7 seconds.

Competitors were not run. Section 2 describes them from public documentation. The baseline uses our small e5 embedder without a reranker; commercial systems use larger embedders and rerankers, so they would be stronger than this baseline.
